title: Keep Colab control-plane authentication distinct from workload credentials
summary: Authentication to allocate/control Colab is not the same thing as credentials used by code inside the VM. Likewise, current upstream colab auth is for authenticating the VM to GCP services; it should not be confused with the local CLI's own Colab API authentication strategy. A managed job can have three separate authorities: local Colab control-plane auth, optional VM/GCP auth, and workload secrets such as a model-download token.
evidence_note: Current upstream CLI exposes global auth strategies (for the CLI) and a separate colab auth command for VM/GCP services. Live Gemma jobs separately qualified colab-auth=READY and staged a Hugging Face read token through Secret Broker.
invariants: Name each credential plane explicitly in job design and evidence.
A valid Colab session does not imply the workload has provider/model credentials.
A model/download secret must not be reused as control-plane authentication.
